text: Supplemental Instruction (SI) provides free, collaborative, group study sessions for students taking historically difficult courses. These sessions are hosted by an SI leader who has previously taken the course and excelled. SI sessions encourage active learning, critical thinking, and group problem solving through engaging activities. Attendance at SI sessions is free and voluntary, no registration required! Data shows that students that consistently attend SI sessions (5+) report higher grade point averages than those that do not attend. Announcements about SI are made in SI-supported courses during the first week of classes and throughout the semester in SI specific course shells. SI sessions begin the third week of classes and continue throughout the semester. SUPPORTED COURSES BECOME A LEADER

‹ 1 › Tips to Succeed in Supplemental Instruction. Bring your lecture materials, textbook, and/or notes to your SI sessions to help you when you get stuck. SI Leaders aren’t lecturers, so be ready to participate and review the materials from class. You will be working collaboratively with other students from their course and will discover new ways to process and study the information in an engaging and welcoming environment. SI is most beneficial when attended regularly. On average, students that attend SI for 5 or more sessions see a 0.5 increase in their grade compared to students who don’t attend SI!
